This game is pure RNG and takes essentially zero strategy or skill. Losing a run almost never felt like it was my fault, it always felt like it was due to an unlucky bounce (most of these were almost instantaneous deaths even though the board was completely stacked with pegs) or an unlucky board layout. The physics feel really wonky, the ball is always moving super fast and bouncing in directions that don't feel intuitive. You get no rewards for losing a run, so unless you're winning, you're literally wasting your time. I'm a massive roguelike fan, but this was not it for me.

9/9/25 update: put a good bit more time into the game after several updates since the original release. saving has been implemented since i played back in march, and i haven't experienced any crashes since, which is nice; however, the fundamental gameplay problem persists: you're still too often at the mercy of shop/ball physics RNG at the beginning of any run; and even when you do gain some early momentum, a bit of bad luck with peg layouts and even worse luck rerolling (jumbling) them can end anything less than an absolutely game-breaking run in seconds. it's just not very fun after multiple bad starts to have to keep mindlessly clicking to the first shop to see if it's worth continuing. i appreciate that the sole developer has been continuing to put work into the game, and i wouldn't ever say that it's gone to waste, especially given how positive the reviews continue to be in general. but for anyone looking for a quick distraction that you don't have to commit a lot of time to in a single run, there's a lot of great budget games to consider, and i'd argue that many do a better job of preventing you from crashing and burning so early and so frequently, especially when it's through very little fault of your own. i'll keep hoping that the rng/difficulty gradient is smoothed out in future updates - the whole package is very charming and creative aside from that core flaw. ================================= original review: an addicting gameplay loop that's too often ruined by mediocre item and perk balance, resulting in a majority of runs either losing with a mishmash of useless and non-synergizing loadouts, or winning on cruise control at 9999x multiplier without even aiming. uninteresting challenges. lack of saving of any kind means that you'll lose your entire run if the game crashes, which has happened three times so far in five hours of gameplay. the framework is there, and the aesthetic is a lot of fun, but the pacing and general balance need a lot of work.

Turns out the game very literally does not have the capabilities to handle the sort of math that the developer throws at you. My regular score was floating well above the quadrillions on average. I fire my Nubby, the game proceeds to throw up an error sign telling me something along the lines of "Cannot divide by zero" and freezes my run and aborts the game, deleting that run and the score with it, forever. Don't make a math based game that can't handle the numbers you make it put out. Incredibly unfortunate that 3 hours and probably the best run anyone will ever have on the game were simply thrown into the trash because the developer wasn't up to the task.

[h1]Nubby's Number Factory[/h1] 哥布林弹球外壳的小丑牌。 虽然有点简单粗暴但大致上差不多就是这样。这个游戏并不纠结于你需要丢出一个多好的角度来触碰到尽可能多的钉子，重点更在于制作出一个链式联锁然后把它引爆。每个钉子的得分都是2的次方，碰一下会减半，比如撞一下64会加64分然后降为32。游戏目标是获得足够的分数，过关时会结算达成目标的次数转化成金币，比如过关要求是100但你打出了666分就能拿到6枚金币，金币可以买道具。 道具栏里的7个道具可以调整顺序，除此之外还有不能丢弃的“补贴(perk)”，在游戏背景里玩家是来数字生产工厂的新员工。道具和补贴都有不同的触发条件，大致上有以下几种：发球时、球落出池子时、达到过关分数、每过x秒、每触碰x次钉子、撞墙x次，道具会在满足条件时触发，而perk的作用是在满足条件时额外触发道具栏，比如在发球时有50%的概率触发3号位的道具。如果3号位的道具效果很好但触发条件却很困难（比如每过3秒触发1次），就可以加快运转效率打出更高的分数，所以整个游戏最有意思的部分也就是不断调整道具栏制作联锁的过程。 结算次数的同时会不断合成池子里的球并回复生命值（最高5点），但过关分数也会跟着数值水涨船高。道具分为加分型和收割型，加分型是“使池子中的球倍数升高”，收割型是召唤各种东西来触发钉子收获分数，没有加分型道具纯靠池子里固有的分数到中期连过关都很困难，但能翻再多倍大分数的钉子卡在下层只靠发球死活打不到也是白搭。所以这游戏最关键的节点就两波，第一波是前期目标分数只有两三位数时，靠多次触发过关+300分的奶酪这类前期道具一下叠出几倍甚至几十倍爆金币滚起雪球，然后就是等好用的诅咒道具。比较稳定的就是”复制第一个碰到的钉子“跟”如果碰到的第一个钉子为池中最大则翻倍结算“。每条命都有一次重置池子排布的机会，只要脸不太黑就已经稳稳过关了，当然也可以像其他rogue-build一样利用道具相互运转实现无限。有个非常搞笑的地方就是到了游戏后期经常不知道整个反应最关键的一环到底在哪里，有钱又不能不花，想替换道具经常裁员裁到大动脉上然后瞬间暴毙。 但我一直觉得rogue最大的乐趣是”尝试用不同的build过关“，这个游戏很有趣，但距离这种苛求的理想境界可能还有一段距离，在打了”上限10金币“和”无法回复生命值“这两个挑战后更加坐实了这一点。游戏没有中文，但道具加一起也就二三十种你查查单词也该记住了，狂野抽象的画风非常欧美meme，可能无法满足颜值党的口味。 LuGN: 7.5/10

虽然内容没有那么丰富，但数值上可谓是弹球游戏的教科书。重点就在于这个“给球”机制的处理。 游戏里有一个机制，每次过关都奖励1次球池数值升级和1金币，如果本关分数超额多倍达成了目标，就多倍获得球池升级与金币。 起初，我发现越后期给的球池基础数值越高，类似于2048后期都是直接给大数字。于是我就想，只要每把的得分倍率超过一个阈值，那我岂不是会打成稳定的指数级成长？当我的成长超过关卡成长、越拉越大，最后是不是有机会达到一万倍？ 不过这件事并没有发生，分析看来，给的球应该是跟关卡层级有关，跟玩家自身的球池进度无关。而就是这样一个简单的设计，直接让整套数值系统让成立了。 即使玩家前期打出成千上万倍，只要后续无法一直维持这几千倍、回归了普通的几十倍甚至几倍，那么随着关卡层级升高，玩家的球池强度迟早会由于“数值膨胀”而趋于普通。每当玩家的球池强度试图超出合理难度数值范围，只需几轮层数膨胀，这个机制都会快速把玩家拉回正常区间。如此一来，游戏给了玩家一种暂时性的能打破游戏的假象（切实让玩家爽到了），但游戏并没有承担玩家滚雪球打破难度平衡的弊端，心流上一直拉扯玩家。除此之外，也能让前期发育得不好的局面，只要苟活下去，在后期照样有机会追平游戏难度。 我倾向于将这种巧思实现的效果称为“自平衡”。这也让我联想到了自走棋的全体玩家抢一个池子的“自平衡”功能。在这款游戏里，无论玩家前期攒了多大的球池，最后几关都是众生平等、趋于平静。玩家能平白无故额外获得大量视听爽感与经济奖励、而不破坏后期平衡；在自走棋中，一个流派越强、就越多人抢、牌库就越稀释，它的综合强度依旧会被拉回平均线附近（甚至在某些局里几家同行一起被抬走）。玩家们平白无故获得了博弈的乐趣与成型的爽感、而不破坏各流派之间的整体平衡。 所以其实这款游戏的游玩思路是，只要活得下去，发育咋样不用特别急，一直1倍过关也不亏，可以直接奔着能打后期的构筑做。

It's a fun game but it gets boring kind of quickly. I am leaving a negative review only because there is no mixed option. Nubby currently has 97% overwhelmingly positive reviews which I find very weird. For me Nubby's Number Factory is a 7,5/10 game, mainly because of the vibes. The roguelike mechanics aren't that good. Its more about numbers and combos between items than the pachinko mechanics. There are no items/perks that for example make Nubby bounce more or reduce the gravity and stuff like that, physics are sometimes straight up weird and annoying. Player can almost always brute force the same build, and is never punished for that because every build has the same core, doubling/halving the numbers (there are challenges that limit that but only a few). There is hardly any item variety so its almost always just the early game that differs from run to run. Also I've only seen 2 different bosses, Tony and the blood rain, both of them are easily countered by happy seal + tardigide + something to pop the numbers combo. The games only difficulty is in the early game and its mostly rng. early game centered items don't really combo with eachother, they are mostly perk depended. Late game is always a steamroll with 9999x round goal score. There are different supervisors that are supposed to change up the game (like characters in Issac or Decks in Balatro) but most of them are literally played the same once you pass round 40 (final boss is on round 80 and after then the player can decide to go endless). There are also special pegs that have special effects but they also don't matter at all since many good late game builds (mainly just 1 build which is always good) just straight up clear entire board anyway no matter what the situation, also there is no way to avoid hitting them since Nubby bounces unpredictably and there are no items to affect Nubbys movement. Game is carried by vibes, but its a chill experience once you get through the early rounds. It's a fun game for a couple of runs or if someone is bored and wants a cheap game to just watch the numbers go brrr. I don't recommend buying it for someone interested in a challenge or for someone who is looking to create fun strategic builds.

game has good bones... but suffers on a bunch of game design issues: 1. every youtube video you watched someone else play was on a different version. the creator of the game decided to nerf/change a bunch of things so overall its not as fun or representative of the videos you saw. 2. after playing this game and running through challenges/trials -- it has one big flaw which is that is that this game ends up being all about RNG. you can't pass certain challenges or trials unless you hope to be lucky enough to get the specific perks and items you need to pass a challenge. 3. once you figure out the formula, you end up playing the same and working around RNG. for example, early +score items early on get you money but are useless after round 40 or so. so you play until you get the key +score items in the first rounds, and give up/restart if you don't because its not worth trying with no way to make money. you end up picking the same key items over and over again because they are consistent. would be nice not to force yourself down the same path most of the time. 4. creator/dev didnt seem to get the memo but there are a ton of terrible "rare" and "ultra-rare" perks and items. perhaps you should keep stats of what people are taking and winning/losing with just so you can see how terrible some of these items/perks are. suggestions: - common/rare/ultra-rare items should rotate on different items. price costs likely should adjust as a result (maybe even effects) - rare/ultra-rare items probabilities are far too low to make any difference in most runs. even when they pop up, they are often garbage items/perks. - many rare/ultra-rare items need to be made significantly better. - nerfing everything = anti-fun. - so many items are outclassed by cheaper/better alternatives. like why bother with expensive crazy straw which is so much worse than pants - upgrade effects for many items seem a bit lazy. IMO the upgrade should be better than the effects of the same item being duplicated - time based triggers are awful since you made pregnancy test so difficult to get. it blows my mind that there are zero items that manipulate the speed of nubby to encourage longer runtimes i think this game would be more enjoyable just entirely getting rid of rarities

The game functioned pretty well, but then the new swathe of items were added. Increasing the size of the item pool without increasing your ability to influence what items you find makes it harder to assemble a specific synergy, and because most synergies are fairly fragile (functionally requiring >6 specific items when you account for getting rank twos, plus a swathe of perks) this makes most synergies unviably difficult to get online. The items themselves are fine, its just the way they interacted with the rest of the game caused the strategic depth of the game to decrease. The challenges and nubby trials are point blank a terrible experience, with the EnHaNcEd DiFfICuLtY just further crushing build diversity. You load in and know there is exactly one viable build, and that you will simply lose repeatedly until you can force it, which for the above mentioned reasons is unreasonably difficult to do. Most of the supervisors are play-once forgettable. Overall the more i played the more I soured on the game, but I did get a decent amount of hours out of it, and you might find you enjoy it.

Nubby really captures a unique charm that satisfies all my different itches. Peggle meets Balatro, it's less (but not none!) about the precision of your shots and rather coming up with builds that work together to really scale those numbers. Surprisingly immersive world full of uncanny and weird, but also charming aesthetics. That finger puppet looks like it could be from one of the Mascot Horrors that have been recently popular, but this game does not have any horror aspects to it. Vinegart did outstanding with the soundtrack, and you can check it out on bandcamp too. This game is surprisingly comforting once you're in a flow state. Nubby is like a pet, beloved and cherished, but sometimes I have actively thought "piece of ♥♥♥♥" when Nubby bounces Perfectly Wrong. But we still love Nubby.

I cannot recommend this game enough it's supa cool. Howeva after playing for a certain amount of time (and will continue to do so) I have my thoughts PROS: - really interesting visual style and fantastically done overall - I always find myself wanting to boot it up again to play more - The different supervisors provide a nice switch-up in gameplay style - You can find builds with items that you get used to, providing unique play styles per person - Well-made music, doesn't get annoying despite how often you'll hear it. That means it's pretty good CONS: -Unlike other plinko games, no real strategy when it comes to launching nubby. He just sort of goes wherever when he bounces. Most times you will lose within the first 20 rounds from bounce RNG - The challenges can be quite hard. There's a reason why the amount of players who have gotten past all the nubby trials is so low. Maybe this could be fixed by allowing the player to choose which supervisor they would like, given that supervisor perks don't clash with the aim of the challenge. (E.G. C.E.O. tony wouldn't be able to be used on the 10 coin challenge). - The main currency is stars, you get 5 for beating a run, a couple less for getting through some of it. A run takes around 15-20 mins. If you wanted to get every nubby skin (that is able to be bought) for the achievement it would cost 850 stars. This would set you back a cool 170 runs (assuming you didn't mess up or need to restart- highly unlikely) totalling a minimal ~42 hours of playtime. For item skins, 117 runs / ~29 hours. On top of that, the ~11 hours to buy every supervisor. You can beat the challeneges for slightly more stars, but again, they will take far more tries to win than the average run. For a plinko game I can imagine this can get a bit soul destroying after a while --------------------------------------------------- Again I CANNOT OVERSTATE how much I like this game!!! This good game!!! yes!!! I hope it continues to be updated in the future too :) You should get it, I mostly made this to outline how difficult it will be if you're someone who likes to 100% complete games.

This is easily the most fun I've ever had playing a roguelike, yes even more so than Balatro. It just does everything right the style, the items and the charm is oozing from this game. It plays like Balatro, Peggle and a 80's macintosh computer had a baby. The one and only problem I have with it is that after 15-20 hours of play it starts to feel a bit stale, because there aren't as many items as I wish there was. But it makes up for that by having extra supervisors (apply special effects to each run) cosmetic unlockables (no microtransactions, you gain meta currency from doing good in runs) and special challenges to put your push your Nubby to it's limits. Tldr; 9/10 could use more item diversity but, has so much fun to be had.
